properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 15 at 8:59PM AKST until November 16 at 1:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulations
between 5 and 10 inches, with up to 12 inches through Turnagain
Pass, and ice accumulations around a light glaze.

* WHERE...Interior Kenai Peninsula, Skilak Lake, and Turnagain Pass.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Monday morning commute. Roads, and especially
bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
Heavy wet snow and ice accumulations could lead to power outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will continue through this evening before
warmer air begins to move over the region, transitioning
precipitation to rain/snow showers. There is a chance (30-40%) for
isolated pockets of freezing rain to linger in typically colder
areas along the Seward Highway from Turnagain Pass to Primrose.
properties.instruction:

* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Additional snow accumulations
up to 2 inches and ice accumulations around a light glaze.

* WHERE...East Turnagain Arm, including Portage Valley and Girdwood.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM AKST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Roads, and especially
bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
Light ice accumulations may result in a few localized power
outages.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Warm air aloft is transitioning snow to rain
showers. As surface temperatures are below freezing in many
locations, falling rain may freeze on contact and create icy
surfaces. Surface temperatures are unlikely to warm above freezing
overnight, so the Advisory has been extended to Monday afternoon,
when surface temperatures will be warm enough to end the threat of
icing from freezing rain.

- 3 inches possible. Winds could gust as high as 65 mph, reducing
visibility to one quarter mile or less.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, Nunivak Island, Good News Bay and
Platinum

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Very strong winds could

quarter mile or less due to blowing snow.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong Bering storm arrives at the Southwest
Coast on Tuesday, bringing a long duration of gusty southerly
winds. Temperatures are expected to warm Wednesday morning,
allowing for a transition to mixed precipitation.
properties.instruction:

potential for falling and/or blowing snow with strong winds and
extremely poor visibilities. This can lead to whiteout conditions and
make travel very hazardous.

properties.instruction:

alert for later statements or warnings, and take action to
protect property.

* WHERE...Atka and Adak.

* WHEN...From 6 PM Monday to 6 AM AKST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel will be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The strongest winds are will be over Adak,
with wind gusts as high as 80 mph, with Atka winds expected to see
gusts to 60 mph. Winds rapidly increase in strength late Monday
evening and peak early Tuesday morning as a strong low pressure
system moves through the Bering. Winds will gradually lighten but
remain gusty through Wednesday.
